loc.1.0:
You entered the elevator and looked around. Your field of view took in the floor, ceiling, double door, and three walls, with a control panel on one of them. There were only four buttons on the control panel. You probably need the top button, because the second and third buttons are labeled "Barracks". Ending up there would be as dangerous as being thrown into outer space without a spacesuit.

You pressed the top button, but the elevator didn't move. Rather, the control panel began to flash: "Access card required". Unfortunately, you don't have an access card and you have nowhere to get one. Neither do you have time to think. Soldiers could appear at any moment. You went into a rage and banged on the control panel to vent your anger. To your surprise, something in the control panel cracked and its hinges swung open. You peered inside and saw a tangle of colored wires. After a close examination, you determined that two bundles of wires were responsible for lifting the elevator to the top level. If you try to connect them the right way, you could probably make the elevator go up even without an access card. The important thing is do this as quickly as possible, before somebody finds you with broken equipment.
loc.2.0:
There are two bundles of wires before you. They are responsible for lifting the elevator to the level with the command room. Each wire has a tiny identification label. Only wires with identical labels should be connected. Moreover, the floor display has turned into a countdown timer. You don't want to think about what will happen when the time runs out.
What are you going to do?

loc.2.2: You looked at the wire's label and saw a <clr>yellow circle<clrEnd>.
loc.2.3: You looked at the wire's label and saw a <clr>red triangle<clrEnd>.
loc.2.4: You looked at the wire's label and saw a <clr>green diamond<clrEnd>.
loc.2.5: You looked at the wire's label and saw an <clr>orange oval<clrEnd>.
loc.2.6: You looked at the wire's label and saw a <clr>white star<clrEnd>.
loc.2.7: You looked at the wire's label and saw a <clr>black dot<clrEnd>.
loc.2.8: It seems you connected the wires correctly. You can continue working.
loc.3.0: Which of the wires do you want to check?
loc.3.1: Which of the wires do you want to connect?
loc.10.0: You messed around with the wires too long. A heavy hand came to rest on your shoulder and a threatening voice advised you to not resist. You tried to escape but did not succeed. Unfortunately, your mission has failed.
loc.11.0: Now you need to choose a wire from the second bundle.
loc.14.0: Apparently, you weren't able to connect all of the wires correctly. As soon as the last pair of wires was connected, sparks flew from the panel and the insulation began to burn. This elevator won't be going anywhere anymore, so you can go surrender yourself.
loc.15.0: You've almost run all the way to the entrance of the command room, but before breaking in there you need to first solve all the problems in this corridor.
loc.15.1: You exerted yourself and kept to the edge of the path, but you were unable to displace your enemies - far too many of them had amassed on the path. While you complained about your misfortune, they caught up to you and began kicking you with their heavy boots.
loc.15.2: You gathered all your strength and took to the path with everything you had. Losing his equilibrium, the enemy running toward you fell and hit his head right on the corner of an old dresser from the Chippendale era with strange markings and gilded inserts. Judging by his rolling eyes and wheezing, he's no longer your enemy.
loc.15.3: You ran up to an enormous curtain that hung near one of the walls and which served as part of the exposition. You began wrapping yourself up in it clockwise. Unfortunately, your enemy didn't embrace the idea of playing hide-and-seek rather than fighting - and kicked you out of your little home.
loc.15.4:
You ran up to an ancient rock fireplace and used your hand to grab one of the burning-hot pieces of coal that were peacefully smoldering in the furnace. This clearly wasn't the best idea you ever had, because the scorching lump of coal began to burn a hole through your hand. You screamed in agony and started hopping up and down. Seeing this sight, the enemy attacking you stopped, his mouth falling open. You decided to pretend that your impromptu behavior was premeditated and tossed the piece of coal right into the soldier's mouth.
He reflexively closed his mouth, but after a moment smoke began issuing from his nostrils and ears, and his eyes doubled in size. Thus smoking, he ran off somewhere toward the elevator, probably in search of a fire hose. Apparently, he has entirely lost interest in you.
loc.15.5: You grabbed the plant and raised it over your head. However, shaking the flowers caused a blanket of pollen to pour onto you and you began to sneeze mercilessly. This threw off your aim and the plant ultimately missed your enemy, but his fists hit their target with precision.
loc.15.6: You grabbed some protruding part of the bulky device and lobbed it at the enemy. It flew at its target, gaining speed, but halfway there it suddenly dropped to the ground with a crash, like a battered bomber airplane, and scattered into pieces. You probably should have unplugged it first, but it's too late to be sorry about that. Unfortunately, the enemy didn't even try to save the rarity, focusing instead on throwing a knife at you.
loc.15.7:
You dodged the enemy's blow, and another - then, in order to avoid being hit, jumped into a large box upholstered with some purple material, which said in large letters: "Houdini". You had just made it inside when the door of the box slammed closed behind your back with a bang, and you felt slightly dizzy. How great was your surprise when, after plowing through the door, you found yourself in an entirely different end of the corridor and the box behind you imploded and disappeared.
Unfortunately, your mysterious teleportation didn't especially impress your enemy.
loc.16.0: As soon as you connected the last pair of wires, the elevator doors closed and it started from its place, lifting you upward. Apparently, you did everything right.
loc.18.0:
You are inside a military base. It differs strikingly from the pirate base on which you've been traveling up to this point. The interior is clean and sparkling. There is no rust anywhere. The information panels are hung carefully. Without moving, you determined that in order to get to the command room you will have to pass through the docking hangar and the main corridor, which is protected by military guards, and then go into the elevator and try to get up to the top level, where the command of this military operation is actually located. Fortunately, the military base is smaller in size. But you mustn't wander about the corridors for hours, because every minute counts.

The important thing to remember is that the military base is packed with soldiers and officers, so you'll never succeed in killing them all as you go. Your only hope is subtlety, ingenuity, and some other obscure word you heard in a joke once: intellect.
loc.19.0:
You took a final look at the familiar, beloved walls of the pirate base and then decisively turned away and marched forward. The hangar proved to be empty, so you made your way through it without trouble. However, you noticed a watchman at the entrance. An immense, muscular maloq is energetically yawning as he sits on a small stool, which is creaking violently under his weight. He doesn't seem very smart.
There are no other exits to the hangar, so decide what you are going to do quickly.
loc.19.1: You hid behind a container near the entrance, having decided to wait a while in the hope that the maloq would become utterly bored and leave. Unfortunately, the stool continued to creak and the maloq kept yawning and yawning, but he never abandoned his post. Finally, his eyes closed tightly and he began to snore loudly. However, you had only managed to take a step toward him when the stool under the watchman collapsed with a crash and the sleeping maloq smashed into the floor. Naturally, he then woke up, sat down on a different stool, and continued to yawn idly.
loc.19.2: You held your breath and tried to sneak past the maloq through a small gap between his back and the wall. Unfortunately, you were only able to get within two meters of him before he turned his head and looked directly at you. Apparently, he didn't at all expect to see someone in a ranger uniform, because he froze in place, dumbfounded, with an open mouth. You need to do something about the situation quickly.
loc.20.0: You adjusted your uniform and marched decisively toward the maloq, knitting your brows severely and blowing out your cheeks slightly for effect. The maloq gawked at you, his mouth open with surprise, while the stool under him is creaking and groaning. You had better act while you can before he starts wondering where you came from.
loc.22.0:
You began screaming wildly and rushed to attack the maloq across half the hangar. The watchman choked on his latest yawn and jumped up from his seat, trying to determine the source of the noise. Upon seeing you, he broke into an ugly grin and threw his jacket on the floor, revealing muscles like large rocks.
The first move you decided to try on the maloq was your master kick, which you quietly named aloud: "Chime of bells". Unfortunately, you had just run within attacking range and began to be threatening, when the maloq sent you to the ground with something reminiscent of "Superweight knockdown". After that, no matter how you tried, you couldn't pull yourself together and assume a vertical position - and then the soldiers ran in...

loc.23.0:
"Bureau of Administrative Review!" you shouted while still approaching.
The maloq stood at attention and mechanically saluted you.
"What a disgrace!" you roared even louder. You got face-to-face with the maloq and began waving your finger in front of his nose. "I will not tolerate this!"
Mesmerized, the maloq followed your finger. And you suddenly thought up what exactly you wouldn't tolerate.
loc.23.1:
"This is simply inconceivable!" you shouted, flying into a rage. "Mess, dust, filth - all around!"
The maloq passed over the hangar, which beamed with cleanliness, and you detected some doubt in his gaze.
"Uh...err... Can I... see your... papers?" he uttered in starts, the last thing you wanted to hear.
loc.23.2:
"Only one watchman at the docking hangar!" you continued shouting. "This is simply inconceivable! A violation of every rule and regulation!!! No oversight!!!
Hearing your screams, the poor maloq even slightly shrank in size.
"Uh...err... Excuse me, sir... Can I... see your... papers?" he uttered in starts, the last thing you wanted to hear.
loc.23.3:
You pulled your ranger identification card from your pocket in a flashy black cover with the Coalition's logo embossed on the front and waved it in front of the maloq without opening it. 
"Major <Ranger>," you said, jutting out your jaw, "Well done, soldier. Vigilance first."
The maloq smile broadly as if you had just promoted him to become an officer.
loc.23.4:
"Would you believe it?" you said in a hushed voice, gazing at the maloq with a purely honest look, "I was in such a hurry to get to the review that I forgot my manbag with all my papers back on the ship". I'm Major <Ranger>. Every swarokok here knows me - just ask anyone.
You walked around the empty hangar with a stately air and were disappointed to notice that the maloq's face is openly suspicious. Apparently, you aren't very convincing.
loc.23.5:
"Papers, uh...of course," you said, reaching into your pocket, acting as if you would pull out an identification badge. "Just a sec...huh? And just what is that?!
You pulled your empty hand out of your pocket and pointed an accusing finger behind the table at the pile of splinters that probably used to be stools.
"They broke..." said the maloq barely audibly, shrinking.
"And what of the inventory!" you screeched. "Government property destroyed! Written off prematurely! Balance the books! The landing area is a disaster! This isn't what I became a major for, dang it!!"
"I won't do it anymore... I..."
"Very well," you said, taking pity on the poor watchman.
loc.23.6:
"What's your name, soldier?" you said, pointing with your finger at the watchman's chest, "And what's your unit number?"
"Private Kicktooth, sir! bellowed the watchman, again standing at full height. "Forty-second company!"
"Excellent. Excellent," you scribbled something on a notepad which you had pulled from the pocket of your coveralls and offered it to him. "Sign here."
"Why?" asked the maloq, beginning to panic. "I mean...sorry. Why, sir?"
"Why?!" you exclaimed, looking at him in surprise, "to document the fact that there was a review."
"Oh...I see," said the maloq pensively, scratching the back of his head. Then he scrawled crookedly across the page.
Your deception seems to have succeeded.
loc.23.7:
"Okay, I'm done here," you said and you took the notepad and pretended to write something on it. Then you read what you had written: "Akhggggglmmvbl"
The maloq tried to glance at the notepad, but you deftly closed it and stuffed it back in your pocket.
"Now, soldier, tell me how to get to the command room," you said, just to be sure you knew the way to go.
"Um... Sorry, sir, but only the high command is allowed in the command room," said the maloq.
You realized that you had blundered, but it was too late to fix your mistake.
loc.23.8:
"Okay, soldier," you said, taking the notepad and poking your finger in the watchman's chest, "now tell me who your commanding officer is."
"Captain Vzgryz, sir," reported the maloq.
"That's explains everything...Vzgryz..." you mumbled as you wrote the name in your notepad. "I remember such a..."
"But why do you need to know, sir?" asked the maloq uneasily.
"What do you mean why?" you asked the watchman in amazement. "To discuss the results of the review with him, of course."
The maloq nodded his head, accepting your response, but you noticed that he was clearly not pleased.
loc.23.9:
"Alright. I'm off," you said to the maloq with a nod. Expecting an irate scream, you took a step toward the exit. Then another and another. You had just begun to want to celebrate when the maloq called out to you:
"Excuse me, sir?! But how did you get into the hangar?"
What bad luck! The maloq proved to be smarter than you thought. You need to respond quickly.
loc.25.0:
"Alright. I'm off," you said to the maloq with a nod. Expecting an irate scream, you took a step toward the exit. Then another and another. Incredibly, you seem to have pulled one on the poor maloq! 
You almost began running, but you restrained yourself at the last minute and walked at an even pace through the hangar doors. The first stage of the operation is behind you.
loc.25.1:
"Listen, little soldier. It'd be better for you to ask yourself that," you shot back at the maloq. "How many of the enemy's units get past you while you're sleeping at your post?"
"Me sleep?" mumbled the maloq.
"What? You've forgotten already?! Of course, if I was zonked out like that, I wouldn't remember much afterward either. So shall I go? Or should I add that when I came to the review the watchman was drooling in his sleep?"
"No, sir," said the maloq in a panic, "please don't write anything in the report. I'll improve!"
"Very well," you agreed graciously and headed toward the exit. 
Incredibly, you seem to have pulled one on the poor maloq! 
You almost began running, but you restrained yourself at the last minute and walked at an even pace through the hangar doors. The first stage of the operation is behind you.
loc.26.0:
Alright. I'm off," you said to the maloq with a nod as you took a step toward the exit.
"Nope. Hold it right there, sir." The maloq's powerful hand came to rest on your shoulder. "I think you've decided to pull a fast one on me."
"Who me?" you said, innocently turning your eyes but panicking inside.
"Yes, sir."
The maloq stuck his hand into your pocket and fished out your ranger identification card. He opened it, looked inside, and chuckled.
"Major, you say? Well..."

You seem to have suffered a devastating and irreversible defeat. You weren't able to fool the dim-witted maloq. Wow!
loc.26.1:
"That's very interesting, because this hangar doesn't have an emergency tunnel, sir," declared the maloq slowly. 
You dashed off, not waiting around to find out what he would say next. But you hadn't taken two steps when a large hand came down on your shoulder and pinned you to the floor.
"Please don't resist."

You seem to have suffered a devastating and irreversible defeat. You weren't able to fool the dim-witted maloq. Wow!
loc.27.0:
Somewhere ahead of you there should be a control point guarded by military patrols. This is the most difficult obstacle on the way to the target, so you must be extremely cautious. 
You passed through two corridors without encountering a soul. All of the doors you've come across on the way have been solidly locked. You stopped for a moment before the next turn in the corridor and suddenly heard voices ahead. There seems to be someone around the corner.
loc.28.0: You moved forward and observed an entire platoon of soldiers in front of you. Unfortunately, noticed you very quickly too. You immediately realized that these weren't dim-witted maloqs and that you wouldn't be able to talk your way out of this, because they raised their weapons and opened fire.
loc.29.0: You listened intently to the conversation around the corner and concluded that a guard post was actually located up ahead. You recognized at least {[p48]} different voices. Moreover, by the authoritative tone in one of the voices, you determined that the soldiers were also in company of their commanding officer. Assessing your abilities, you estimated that you could easily handle two soldiers, maybe even three - if you got lucky. But simple tricks won't work with an officer.
loc.29.1: You froze in place and began to bide your time, hoping that nobody would come around the corner and discover you there. You wait for some time, but, based on the sound of it, nothing changed at the guard post.
loc.29.2: While waiting you sharpened your ears and heard a message of the radio announcing that Admiral Durdym requires a bottle of the best champagne be delivered to the command room. Two brave warriors were dispatched to accomplish this difficult mission.
loc.29.3: Not only were the soldiers not diminishing in numbers while you waited, some sort of aide arrived with papers. The soldiers began to argue with him about something and there was the sound of documents rustling, but you weren't able to clearly hear what they were talking about.
loc.29.4: While you waited at the guard post a message was announced over the internal network regarding the possible presence of enemy forces in quadrant B4. A team of three soldiers was immediately dispatched there. You prayed fervently to all the known gods that quadrant B4 might not be located between you and the soldiers and, apparently, somebody heard you. The footsteps of the departing soldiers clattered away from you.
loc.29.5: You had nearly dozed off from boredom when a scream of pain and loud howls awoke you. One of the soldiers had been playing around with a knife and accidentally sliced his palm with the blade. The stupid soldier was sent to the infirmary and warned that the next time he pulled a mindless stunt like that he would be sent to the lock-up rather than the doctor.
loc.29.6: You waited and waited, and waited some more. Then you again waited for a bit, but the enemy's forces weren't getting smaller. On the contrary, yet another soldier, who had running an errand for an officer, arrived at the post. He reported something - you couldn't hear exactly what - and joined the rest of the soldiers.
loc.29.7: Your waiting became much more pleasant with the unexpected departure of the officer. He probably needed to use the restroom, since he left another one of the soldiers in charge and quickly marched off.
loc.30.0:
You decided that there was no point to waiting longer and that it was time to attack. Cautiously slipping out from behind the corner, you surveyed the scene before you with a skillful eye. The corridor ahead was blocked by a small turnstile, which wasn't working for some reason, though this was better for you. An iron cabinet as tall as a person stands off to your right. Immediately behind it is a little table which the soldiers have gathered around. You quickly counted them up - [p48] in all. In the far end of the corridor is an elevator.
You need to think of something to do before the soldiers discover your presence.
loc.35.0: You drew out your knife, screamed something so terribly warlike that you even scared yourself a little, and rushed in to attack. You got lucky and the soldiers didn't immediately understand what was happening. Meanwhile, you managed to wound one of them and tackle another. Finally, your enemies understood what was happening, but it was too late. In half a minute you had already wiped the blood off your blade onto the pants of one of the fallen soldiers. Your ambush seems to have succeeded. How wonderful!
loc.35.1: You strained and brought all your strength to bear on the cabinet. It slowly but surely tipped over, landing on one of the soldiers. While it was falling you pulled out your knife and attacked the others. They couldn't do a thing to resist your mastery of the cold weapon and in half a minute you had already wiped the blood off your blade onto the pants of one of the fallen soldiers. Your ambush seems to have succeeded. How wonderful!
loc.35.2: You flicked a coin into the air and it cheerfully jingled on the tiles of the corridor as it rolled around the corner. The soldiers, seized with excitement, ran by noisily without noticing you at all. Only one soldier remained at the guard post, who was anxiously listening to what was happening around the corner. You leapt out from behind the cabinet and cut him down before he could scream out. Your ambush seems to have succeeded. How wonderful!
loc.36.0: You screamed something so terribly warlike that you even scared yourself a little, pulled out your knife, and launched into a frontal assault of the enemy. You even managed to get a couple of good hits in, but your opponents carried the day. They pressed you into the corner, and pummeled you first with their fists and then with a table, just to make sure. You, a feeble and delicate ranger, couldn't endure such treatment, and died.
loc.36.1: You strained your powerful ranger muscles and pushed into the cabinet. It began to sway and you pushed harder. Slowly but surely, it fell down right on top of the soldiers. Unfortunately, it solidly crushed only one of them, and for some reason the rest of the soldiers very upset with you. They pressed you into the corner, and pummeled you first with their fists and then with a table, just to make sure. You, a feeble and delicate ranger, couldn't endure such treatment, and died.
loc.36.2: You threw a coin and the soldiers ran obediently toward the sound, not noticing you at all. But the officer, who didn't fall for your cheap trick, looked around and immediately discovered your presence. You ran in for the attack, but he proved to be both smart and an expert at one-on-one combat. After bruising you up a bit, he tossed you toward his soldiers. They pressed you into the corner, and pummeled you first with their fists and then with a table, just to make sure. You, a feeble and delicate ranger, couldn't endure such treatment, and died.
loc.36.3: You hurled a coin through the entire corridor and it cheerfully jingled on tile floor. Unfortunately, only one of the soldiers heard the sound. The rest of them turned their heads and discovered your presence. You realized that you had nothing to lose and flew into an attack. But the odds were tipped against you. They pressed you into the corner, and pummeled you first with their fists and then with a table, just to make sure. You, a feeble and delicate ranger, couldn't endure such treatment, and died.
loc.37.0:
The elevator finally reached the top level and gently came to a halt. You prepared yourself emotionally for the fact that anything might be waiting for you. The elevator doors opened and you immediately heard an authoritative voice bark:
"Private Bobson, suck in your gut! It's not dinnertime! Like this! Remember, occupying this post is a great honor and responsibility! The priceless exhibits here belong to Admiral Durdym personally. If anything happened to them, he would shoot you down - at a minimum! Don't even breath when you're walking by them! Not one sp... hmm... Bobson, Shotnag - go check the elevator. Something's not right with it."

The soldiers probably noticed that the elevator doors opened but nobody came out. You need to think of something to do before you're discovered!
loc.38.0:
You pulled out your knife and pressed up against the wall of the elevator, but no matter how hard you tried, your uniform remained a conspicuous spot on the snow-white background of the wall. Thus, when the two soldiers entered the elevator with weapons at the ready, they immediately saw you and opened fire. Bullets ricocheted in every direction, and you jumped out of the elevator. But not quickly enough - one of the bullets pierced your left hand.  
"Cease fire!" screamed the officer desperately, when a stray bullet hit the wall near one of the works of art.
You glanced around and observed that both sides of the corridor in front of you were lined with all sorts of antique junk. Just by looking at them, you can tell that several of the exhibits are wildly expensive. If not for them, you would have been riddled with bullets by now. You need to continue taking advantage of this, because you are unlikely to be able to cope with four enemies.
loc.38.1:
You pulled out your knife and jumped out of the elevator right into two soldiers, who recoiled in surprise but quickly came to their sense and opened fire. Naturally, you didn't wait for them to hit you and began to dodge and evade.
"Cease fire!" screamed the officer desperately, when a stray bullet hit the wall near one of the works of art.
You glanced around and observed that both sides of the corridor in front of you were lined with all sorts of antique junk. Just by looking at them, you can tell that several of the exhibits are wildly expensive. If not for them, you would have been riddled with bullets by now. You need to continue to take advantage of this, because you are unlikely to be able to cope with four enemies.
loc.38.2: A bearded philosopher of old once said, "Motion is life." And it's true - as long as you're running about the corridor you have a chance. But if you stop, the enemy will press you up in a corner and make it hurt.
loc.38.3: You snatched the model ship and were disappointed to discover it was hollow - and didn't weigh much at all. But you couldn't do anything to change that. You hurled the model at your enemy, but he easily caught it and carefully put it on the floor. Immediately after that, he dug into your ribs with the butt of his gun and smashed your jaw with his fist. It hurt a lot.
loc.38.4: You snatched some golden goblet lined with tacky pebbles from a stone pedestal and sent it flying straight at your enemy's head. He threw up his hands to block the blow, but not fast enough. The goblet hit him right in the noggin. The soldier's eyes rolled back and he thudded to the ground unconscious. The fact that the collision with his head protected the goblet from harm won't be comforting to him when he regains consciousness.
loc.38.5: Your knife dance ended poorly. The enemy, on the other hand, tricked you with a fake move. And instead of stabbing him, you took a blow from his knife. This proved to be very painful.
loc.38.6: You grabbed the aquarium, strained all your muscles, held your breath, and...couldn't make it budge. With the water it was just too heavy. Exotic fish looked at you reproachfully from behind the glass. But when the butts of the soldiers' guns came down on your back, the fishes' mood brightened remarkably.
loc.38.7: You seized a large, decorative umbrella from a mannequin's hand and hid behind it when you saw that your enemy was about to throw a knife at you. Unfortunately, the old material didn't save you and the knife passed through it like an unlucky ranger would pass through a gobzaurus's esophagus. Though undeniably faster. The knife pierced your collarbone, causing unthinkable suffering.
loc.38.8: You grabbed a long, striped lance from a knight mannequin, which was part of an exhibit on ancient Earth, and rushed to attack your enemy. But you weren't used to the weapon and it stuck into the floor, and you flew over the stunned soldier like a high jumper, landing in the middle of the corridor. The lance hit the soldier on the head, but not very hard, and he only rubbed the back of his head before charging at you again.
loc.39.0: As long as you're running, it's harder for your enemy to catch you, which means you have a greater chance of success.
loc.39.1: You jumped up to the dresser and tugged with all your might on the drawers, but not one of them would give. Meanwhile, your enemy got within striking distance and began to hit you painfully with the butt of his gun.
loc.39.2: 0.314 seconds. That's how long you admired a delicate, handmade vase of beautiful craftsmanship. Then you swung around and smashed it into your enemy's head, at the same time realizing that it was produced in the period of the Bdzyn dynasty. Indeed, that was the type of sound it emitted as it disintegrated into small shards. You wanted to share this joyous discovery with your enemy, but he was already out cold and couldn't congratulate you on your archaeological triumph.
loc.39.3: You removed a famous painting by the artist Reheuza Pin from the wall and used it as a shield. By tragic coincidence, your enemy hurled a knife at you precisely at this moment. When the sharp tool ripped a hole through the middle of the painting, the soldier sat down and began to tremble in anticipation of the admiral's reprisal. You tossed the useless painting aside and wipe the blood off your cheekbone, where the knife had grazed you, and felt great relief that it hadn't hit you in the eye.
loc.39.4: Your enemy howled in horror and jumped to save the painting, which was flying straight for the sharp horns of a poochercorn. He managed to grab the painting at the last second, letting it fall gently to the floor, but impaling himself on a sharp horn in the process. You never would have done such a stupid thing, even if the painting was worth millions of banknotes. And it doesn't make any sense for there to be a stuffed poochercorn here, because there are roughly a million animals in the universe that are more beautiful and rare.
loc.39.5: "Is this some sort of galactic circus?!" you thought when you saw how your enemy skillfully catch every bottle you threw in his direction. To your temporary circus partner's credit, he succeeded in catching everything you threw at him, even the last bottle, which was thrown off to the right with a special twist. You were involuntarily filled with respect for the soldier's appetite for life. After all, if even one of the bottles broke, the admiral would have his head.
loc.39.6: You picked up a thick old book from a richly decorated desk and threw it toward your enemy, but it broke into pieces midflight. It looked several hundred years old, but now you let it depart in peace to a long-awaited rest. But what are you talking about? It was just an ordinary book, not some ancient old guy.
loc.41.0:
You surveyed the field of battle and observed that none of your enemies showed any sign of life and that most of the precious exhibits were destroyed to some degree or another. Not that this matters. The only thing left for you to do is go into the command room and deal with the admiral. After that he probably won't worry about his collection very much.
You approach the door and were just about the open it when it opened on its own and you were met by a scraggly soldier in full military uniform, though he was clearly not the boss. His chest obviously lacked medals and his shoulder insignia had no stars. This must be one of the admiral's aides.
- ...! He wanted to scream, but you quickly covered his mouth with your hand.
loc.43.0:
You instantly snapped the admiral's assistant's puny neck and quietly laid his body on the floor in front of the entrance, not forgetting to keep his blaster as a souvenir of your brief meeting. Then you rummaged through the pockets of the deceased, but didn't find anything useful in them.
Strange as it may seem, the long and difficult road is behind you - and you're still alive. That means you can begin the final stage of your mission - the extermination of the head of the military operation.

param.1.crit:
You fought bravely and selflessly. However, the odds were too much in favor of the enemy. After picturesquely falling on your knees, you clutched one hand against your chest and thrust the other toward the stars, which unfortunately were not visible because of the ceiling, and cried out:
"Pirates! Coalition! I'm dying! A plague on both of your houses!
Then you fell on your face and ceased to show any sign of life.

param.49.crit: You continued to wait, but luck was against you and a soldier, who was apparently trying to get to the restroom, came around the bend, directly in front of you. Having discovered you, he immediately yelled loudly for help and began attacking with his bare fists. You began to defend yourself, but just then the remaining soldiers arrived and you were quickly overpowered. Thus your triumphant crusade for glory came to an unexpected and ignominious end.
